verdict.rationale: Meilisearch's own docs describe a hybrid search capability that combines full-text keyword matching with semantic matching, with embeddings generated automatically once an embedder is configured. The evidence does not show how the two result sets are fused or weighted, or that both run in one search request; it only says 'a single API'. There is no hands-on or independent confirmation, so the story's single-query fusion element is unproven. missing for 10: documented single-request hybrid query syntax, fusion/weighting mechanism (e.g. a semantic-vs-keyword ratio), independent or hands-on corroboration of hybrid queries.

support.subject: As a developer, I can run hybrid search — semantic vector similarity fused with keyword matching — in a single query

citations.quote: Hybrid search combines two search strategies: full-text search (matching keywords) and semantic search (matching meaning).
When you configure an embedder, Meilisearch automatically generates vector embeddings for every document in your index.
Combine keyword precision with AI that understands meaning and intent.
exposes them through fast full-text search, semantic search, and conversational interfaces, all from a single API
